newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN PM ASKS RENAULT TO RETHINK PLANT CLOSURE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN PM ASKS RENAULT TO RETHINK PLANT CLOSURE.

text.p: Belgium on Thursday asked French car maker Renault to rethink its decision to close an assembly plant in Vilvoorde near Brussels, a move which will lead to the loss of over 3,000 jobs.

In a letter to Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said he hoped the Frenchman was considering other solutions, and he pointed to new benefits approved by his government for firms being restructured.

"I draw your attention to measures the Belgian government has just approved which let companies going for restructuring and shorter working hours benefit from a substantial cut in employers' social security charges," Dehaene said in his letter.

Introducing a 32-hour week at the Vilvoorde plant would save 200 million Belgian francs worth of social charges on an annual basis, he said. This represented a fall of four percent in hourly wage costs.
The Belgian Prime Minister had already condemned the closure plan, and the harsh way it was announced.
Commenting on the closure, Belgian employers have pointed the finger at the country's high labour costs. Between 1987 and 1996 these have risen by 4.2 percent, outpacing neighbouring countries.

Workers from the Vilvoorde plant took part in protests at Renault factories in France on Thursday and earlier this week joined thousands of other European car workers on a march in Paris in protest at the Belgian closure and planned job cuts in France.
